extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Skeletal system — the framework of bones in the human body. Functions: give shape and support to the body, protect internal organs (skull protects brain, ribs protect heart and lungs), help in movement with muscles. Major bones: skull (protects brain), jawbone (helps chewing), backbone (supports body, made of small vertebrae), chest bone and ribs (protect heart and lungs), arm bones, leg bones. (2) Joints — places where two or more bones meet. Types: hinge joint (elbow, knee — bends like a door hinge), ball and socket joint (shoulder, hip — allows rotation in all directions), pivot joint (neck — allows turning head side to side), gliding joint (wrist — bones slide over each other), fixed joint (skull — bones do not move). (3) Care of bones and posture — drink milk and eat calcium-rich foods (milk, cheese, yogurt, green leafy vegetables), exercise regularly (walking, running, stretching), maintain good posture (sit straight, stand tall, don't slouch), avoid lifting very heavy weights improperly, wear protective gear (helmet while cycling, seatbelt in car), get enough rest and sleep on a firm mattress. Misconceptions: 'bones are dead structures' (WRONG — bones are living tissue that grow and repair themselves), 'the backbone is one single bone' (WRONG — the backbone is made of 33 small bones called vertebrae), 'all joints allow the same movement' (WRONG — different joints allow different movements: hinge bends, ball and socket rotates, pivot turns), 'only old people need to care about bone health' (WRONG — bone health starts from childhood; calcium and exercise in childhood build strong bones for life), 'poor posture only affects appearance' (WRONG — poor posture can cause back pain, spinal problems, and affect breathing and digestion).
